text: player
Chiori Mikami
Riu Kujou
I've seen the answer to this question before on CatChat... If my memory serves me right, it is... Ah! I've found it!
Yes, it's this one! Chiori replied to Reina on CatChat at that time, and the answer is Mandheling coffee beans!
...You're not allowed to check your mobile phone for the next question!
Question two. What is Miss Chiori's favorite animal?
Isn't it obvious? She loves bears the most. I can tell because her handbag is literally a bear!
A flash of surprise appears on Chiori Mikami's face, whereas Riu Kujou remains calm like always.
I see... It's too easy for you to guess the answer if I only give you two options. In that case... what about this question?
Question three. What is the name of Miss Chiori's bear handbag?

Riu Kujou lowers her head and jots down some words quickly. She then shows me a piece of paper with five names to choose from... That's right... five. It looks like she really doesn't want me to answer the question correctly.
Riu Kujou rejects my request and continues to send a series of questions about Chiori Mikami in my direction.

The good news is that I'm really lucky today and managed to answer the questions correctly even when I was just guessing. The bad news is that Riu and Chiori forced me to leave the café while I was feeling smug. I could only watch helplessly as the cup of coffee that Reina Nanami had just brought to the table, made with new special blend coffee beans that I hadn't gotten the chance to taste, got further and further away from me...

Outside the pure white window sill, slender green trees sway gently, their fluffy canopies letting generous patches of light through their gaps and creating a contrast of light and shadows on the clean wooden floor. Marvelous bookcases that occupy an entire wall are filled with various books, while calligraphy works and paintings of celebrities adorn the wall. The style of her study suggests this young lady's interests go far beyond just cuteness.

However, Riu Kujou's powerful gaze makes me withdraw my curious gaze from where I am sitting on the sofa. Just now, Chiori Mikami said she needed to prepare some items, so she asked Riu Kujou to take me to this study and fill me in on the details while I wait for her.
If it weren't for the fact that I'm in the middle of my final exams for the special maid training class, you would never get this opportunity.
...Opportunity?
Yes, an incomparably valuable opportunity to be Miss Chiori Mikami's teammate! To be specific, one day ago...
What a familiar way to start talking about past memories... Ah!
DON'T INTERRUPT ME!
Every iron fist Riu Kujou sends my way is a reward I've earned with my abilities. Riu Kujou continues speaking while I rub my head and nod vigorously.

...One day ago, Miss Chiori and I went to a board game parlor because she heard that the parlor had just stocked a new board game that is played in teams of two and wanted to try it out. Miss Chiori should have won the game easily since she is so intelligent, but we played against a lovey-dovey couple. In the end...
Miss Chiori, we... lost.
...Damn! I only need a few more moves to catch up to their pieces!
Couple Opponent A
Hahaha, don't look so depressed, little girl. This board game that is played in teams of two is a test of the teammates' synergy, especially their synergy in terms of feelings.

You look like a junior high school student, and the maid next to you, well, doesn't seem to have much experience... Umm, if neither of you has ever been in a relationship or had anyone confess their love to you, then you're already really amazing to play this well! Isn't that right, babe?
Couple Opponent B
Yes! Everything you say is right, darling!
Hmph! Don't look so pleased. This is just a temporary defeat. Give me two days! Two days is all I need! We just need one day to practice, then we'll be able to defeat you!
Hahaha, okay then. I'll be looking forward to it.

That's basically what happened. Miss Chiori has arranged a rematch with them tomorrow, but my special maid training camp exam is scheduled for tomorrow, so I can't go with her, which means I need to find her a suitable board game teammate.

Does that mean the survey in the café is part of your test to find a suitable teammate? I'll be honest with you, to answer those questions correctly, you just need to know a little more about Chiori than most people. What does that have to do with synergy?

Oh, the purpose of those questions is to select a teammate who is lucky enough and understand Miss Chiori's likes and dislikes enough to keep her in a good mood. As for the synergy, Miss Chiori said she'll train you personally.
Train... Fine then, but can you please not use any strange verbs so casually?
I'm back!
As she speaks, Chiori Mikami enters the study with a box.
Do you understand everything now?
Yes, I know what's going on.
But... I'm a little hesitant. However, Chiori Mikami continues speaking without giving me the chance to organize my thoughts.
Okay, Riu, you can study for your exam now. Leave the rest to me. I'll train a qualified teammate to avenge yesterday's loss!
Yes! You have my full trust, Miss Chiori! You can do it! I'll be going back to my room then. Just call for me if you need anything.
You need to try hard and do well too, or else...
As Riu Kujou speaks, she warns me by waving her fist at me and leaves reluctantly after I start nodding repeatedly.
Chiori Mikami and I are now the only people in the room. Before I can speak, she quickly opens the box she just brought in and thrusts a booklet in front of me.
Here you go. Read this before we start the training.
It turns out that this is a board game, and what she just gave me is its manual. I swallow the words of hesitation I was about to voice and read it carefully.

In this game called "Heart Map," teams of two need to explore the game board that has an extremely complex terrain, and the first team to reach the destination at the end of the map wins. This game relies on the tacit cooperation between teammates as whether players move forward or backward, the direction of movement, and the number of steps taken are all determined by the results of the card missions that both teammates encounter along the way.
So it really is like this... Chiori, although we're good friends, don't you think it'll be difficult for us to defeat a pair of lovers who are truly intimate?
After reading the manual, I voice the concerns in my heart. To my surprise, Chiori Mikami reacts very disdainfully.
Who said we need synergy to win?
What's your plan?

Listen up, because I'll only say this once. As long as it is a game, you'll be able to find a way to win if you can master the essence of its rules! In a game like this that requires players to play in teams of two, the rules make it seem like you need synergy, which is invisible and intangible, when what the players really need is to act as one.
Act as one?
Yes! The key to winning isn't how well we know each other. What we need to do is to solve problems in the same way!
Huh? People need to use a secret trick like this to answer those basic questions at school? Are you the One Han City student who you are referring to?
I was just making an example... What I'm saying is that we can think of similar secret tricks to help us solve problems in the same way.

I guess you can think of it in that way, but we need to come up with secret tricks that match the rules of this game, and it's definitely more complicated than what you said. Anyway, let's try playing it first. There are so many questions in this board game!
Hmm...
Why are you in a daze?
Let me see...

According to the manual in front of me, the creator of this board game designed it to help the participants learn more about each other by playing it, but Chiori Mikami has obviously skipped this part.
Hmm, after understanding what needs to be done, I hesitate about whether I want to do this training with Chiori Mikami.

If I play this game that's all about synergy with Chiori by taking advantage of the loopholes in its rules, it seems to take the meaning and fun out of it. Our victory would be hollow even if we did manage to win because we might have missed out on an even richer experience.
Sorry, Chiori, I don't want to do this training.
...Why?
As it probably never occurred to Chiori Mikami that I would turn her down, she looks a little dazed for a moment, then she starts blinking in panic.
Y-You! How dare you to reject me! Do you think that just anyone can get this chance to be my teammate?!
Of course not... But I just read the information and realized that the creator designed this board game to help the participants learn more about each other by playing it.
I don't think we should discuss a strategy in advance because the game wouldn't be fun. I prefer to develop a lasting synergy with you, Chiori.
I express my thoughts carefully with my words because I want Chiori Mikami to understand my sincerity.
Chiori Mikami looks at me and even seems to be a little moved, but after a brief silence, she makes an aggrieved expression with her beautiful eyes.
...Geez, all you do is preach to me. You aren't even willing to help me win a game. {var:player_nickname}, you really are a jerk, idiot, and nuisance! In that case, I won't play with you anymore!
Eh?!
Chiori turns around angrily and faces me with her sulking back every time I try to explain.
A huge red exclamation mark pops up in my heart. This is a crisis! This is a major crisis in my friendship with Chiori Mikami!
...Oh well, even cats loath being stroked against the hair. After thinking about it, I come up with a possible solution.
It looks like we won't be able to change each other's minds. In that case, Chiori, why don't we decide it with a match?
No!
...Chiori, don't tell me you're afraid of playing against me?
You're the one who is afraid! Well, what should we play?
Phew! At least this trick still works. To some extent, this young lady is quite easy to coax.
Ahem, any game you like. We'll settle it with one match, and the loser has to listen to the winner. What about that?
Okay! Let's do it! I'm going to win!

Two different types of board games, One Han City Monopoly and Kalli Galli, are on the desk in the study, both of which were found by Chiori Mikami when she rummaged through the drawers in the study. They are board games that most youths of One Han City have at home.
To be fair, I'll let you choose which of these two games to play. The winner will be in charge.
They are both popular games, but they are quite different... To win against Chiori Mikami, I need to choose carefully.

The rules of Kalli Galli are: Players play cards with fruits printed on them in turn. When there are five of a certain type of fruit on the table, the player who rings the bell first can take all the cards on the table. The player who wins all the cards from the other player's hand wins the game.

Although the Chiori Mikami I know is a complete demon at the mahjong table, she is like a natural airhead in real life. I'll have a greater chance of winning if I choose a fast-paced board game that relies on reflexes.
I choose Kalli Galli!
As I expected, Chiori Mikami shows a hint of displeasure after hearing this.
...Tsk, you must have been watching me closely for a long time before you found this weakness, right?
You need to know your enemy to win every battle. I won't go easy on you.

As I expected, Chiori Mikami's airheadedness puts her at a disadvantage from the very beginning. Although she watches the number of fruits on the table carefully, I manage to ring the bell before her several times.
Ding!

I ring the bell for a third time and smugly take away all of Chiori Mikami's cards on the table. She blinks while looking at the empty table before realizing that there were already five of a certain fruit on the table. After that, she looks at me unhappily, unwilling to accept her defeat.
This isn't over yet. Keep going!
Thanks for letting me win.
A new battle begins. We both focus on the game and play our cards one by one... Soon, I notice that there are five of the same fruits on the table and prepare to ring the bell. Suddenly--
Hey, look! What's that?
Chiori Mikami suddenly points behind me with a surprised look on her face.
Huh?
...Come on, your hand speed is slower than mine, and I can see through your deception with a glance.
T-Take a look! There really is something!

As she sees my hand get closer and closer to ringing the bell, Chiori Mikami tries her best to make the most exaggerated expression she can manage to try and convince me to believe her nonsense. She is even so anxious that little droplets start to roll out of her eyes. I must say... she looks so cute!
No way... She is willing to resort to such foul tactics to win? Well, I guess the rules don't say that this method can't be used...
In that instant, I start to waver... Should I stop her extremely cute "performance"?
One Han City Monopoly is a classic economic board game. It's a game that almost everyone plays in One Han City, and I'm naturally also very familiar with it.

The map and landmark buildings of One Han City are simulated in this game, and all players start with the same amount of funds. Starting from the Start space, whenever it is their turn, players move a number of steps by rolling a dice. This game requires a mix of luck and trading strategies as players need to buy land and build buildings to earn rent. The game ends when one of the players becomes bankrupt.
I've been really lucky in mahjong recently, and an economic game should give me enough leeway to play steadily and win.
I choose One Han City Monopoly!
...Hehe, what a foolish decision.
To my surprise, Chiori Mikami smiles confidently and disdainfully when she hears my choice, which gives me a bad feeling.
Six... Six...
One... One...

Sunlight dances on the board and the game props on the table. The exquisite plastic dice makes a crisp sound while it rolls on the board, captivating my and Chiori Mikami's attention. We mumble under our breath childishly as we try to change the result psychically.
In the end, my dice twirls around and stops, revealing one red dot... I rolled a one.
Yay! It's a one!
Sigh, okay then. I can only move one step... Huh? Wait a minute, it's a Chance space! Hahahaha!
...Eh? Hmph, whatever. You do seem a little lucky today.
Chiori Mikami's cheers end abruptly as I start grinning happily. I draw a Chance card joyfully and read out its contents.
"You win first place in the Mahjong Soul Shrine tournament and can choose one player to grant a wish for you. If they refuse, they need to pay you 50,000 Coppers."
What?! How can there be such an outrageous card!
Hahaha, this is the only one. It looks like luck is on my side today. Chiori, will you give me 50,000 Coppers or grant one of my wishes?
I'll grant a wish, but don't go too far, or I'll call Riu over right away!
Hmm, let me see... Something that won't be too excessive...
In consideration of her threat to summon her maid, I decide to take Miss Chiori's friendly advice and ask her to grant an innocuous wish.
No way! This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, so I can't stop all the ideas that are popping up in my head... Which one should I choose?
Chiori Mikami, please make me a cup of coffee.
However, Chiori Mikami makes a displeased expression right after I make this request.
Hey, this request isn't too excessive. Didn't you work at Reina's place before?
Phew! I heave a sigh of relief when I see Chiori Mikami get up and go downstairs. It seems that the rules of the game are useful after all.
Here you go.
Chiori Mikami serves me a cup of coffee personally as promised. The cup of coffee served perfectly on a plate is aromatic and has exquisite latte art, which makes me feel a little flattered.
Thank you, Chiori. I'll dig in then.
I raise the cup and take a sip. A spicy taste that doesn't belong to coffee takes me by surprise and rushes straight into my head.
Urgh! Bleurgh! Why is it spicy?!
Hehe, you only asked me to make you a cup of coffee, but you didn't say what it had to taste like. There are no rules saying that you can't add chili powder to coffee, right?
...It's so spicy that I can't speak and tears roll out of my eyes. Chiori Mikami looks at me happily and even takes photos with her phone.
...So this is what this girl who is good at taking advantage of loopholes is capable of? How scary!!!

Chiori Mikami looks at me disdainfully and shakes her head, then she turns around to go to the kitchen and returns with another cup of coffee. However, there are ice cubes floating on the surface this time.
You're so useless. Since we still need to finish this game, you better drink this cup.
It's too late to consider whether this is a normal cup of iced coffee, so I take it and start gulping it down.
The icy cold coffee neutralizes the spiciness the moment it slides down my throat...
Hmph, this is just a small lesson. I won't let you off so easily the next time you take advantage of a similar situation to request me to do something so excessive. Do you understand?
I nod wildly. Thankfully, she still cares about me and didn't set up consecutive traps for me.
We return to the study after this brief wish-making session, which I can't tell is a punishment or reward, ends.
Let's continue playing the game. I'm going to show you my real strength now.
Same here.
I roll the dice gently, after which our pieces continue to fight fiercely on the board.

However, luck becomes less important as the game progresses, and the requirement for players to have good resource allocation, trading and purchasing, business vision, and other capabilities, increase accordingly. To my surprise, Chiori Mikami manages to take all my assets without me realizing it.

Looking at Chiori Mikami who is in full control of the situation and exuding that familiar demon-like aura she has in mahjong dojos, I realize that I had greatly underestimated her mastery of this game.

In the final stage of the game, I try my best to compete for resources and surpass Chiori Mikami, but the scale of victory tilts to the other side. After one last roll of the dice, I roll on a property owned by Chiori Mikami. I look at the small amount of game currency I have left and the taxes I can't afford, then I raise my hands in surrender.
I've lost. You're too good at this, Chiori. It doesn't feel like we're playing a Monopoly game.
Hmph, nonsense. This is what you get for underestimating me.

With a face filled with pride, Chiori Mikami walks to the bookcases in the study and presses something in front of them. In the next second, I hear the sound of mechanical slide rails as the seemingly normal bookcases suddenly move. Some bookcases move to the left, while some other bookcases move to the right, revealing a hidden space behind them!

I am dumbfounded by this scene. When I look over, I see that the hidden space behind the bookcases is filled with various board game gift boxes, chess boards, and board game props of all sizes... This collection room is like heaven to board game players!
You didn't expect this, right? I'm not an ordinary player. If you want to beat me, you need to play as many board games as me first! We're not on the same level at all.
It turns out that Chiori Mikami is not just any ordinary player who goes to board game parlors on a whim. She's a professional board game master!
Hahaha! You're so amazing!
After experiencing a brief shock, I suddenly feel a surge of admiration. This young lady always seems to surprise me.
...Huh?
Chiori Mikami, however, doesn't seem too happy with my reaction. She looks at me with some surprise.
What is it?
You're so strange. You lost and saw the gap between us. Shouldn't you be sad, unhappy, or angry? Just like those... those...

Some images instantly appear in my mind, and they seem to tell me what she wants to say. "Just like those opponents she encounters in dojos or while playing other board games who run away crying after she beats them."
I smile and shake my head.
Although I lost, at least I got to spend an unforgettable afternoon with you, Chiori. This is an unforgettable experience in itself, so why should I be unhappy?

The late afternoon sun shines into the study. The game board and props are still spread everywhere on the table as we haven't gotten around to tidying them up yet. One of the pieces wobbles and falls over as a gust of wind blows into the room, sending ripples through the world of the game board.
Chiori Mikami's eyelashes tremble slightly as she thinks deeply. She turns her head away and mutters something under her breath, then she looks up at me.
We're not going tomorrow. The training is canceled.
Huh? Canceled? Why?

...You idiot. We spent the whole afternoon playing this game. We don't have enough time for the training even if we start now. We'll just lose again if we challenge that couple tomorrow. What's more...

What's more, I've thought about it. {var:player_nickname}, you and I have a different idea of victory. Since we need to play this game as a team, we won't really win if I'm the only one who thinks we've won.
Does this mean you're starting to consider my feelings, Chiori?
T-That's not it! I'm only considering this because you're my teammate!
Oh, I see.
I readily agree. After all, I was lucky enough to see her blushing with embarrassment, so it doesn't matter if her argument is a little weak. Of course, I'll forgive her.
...We'll need to do some real training so that we both win.
Haha, so you're saying that we will win the game and get a perfect score for our synergy? This seems even harder than what you were originally aiming for.
That's why you're not allowed to slack off starting today!
Okay, okay. We'll agree on that happily then.
Chiori Mikami and I then made this agreement. Later, when I looked through her collection of board games carefully, I asked her curiously--
That's right. Chiori, when did you start playing board games?
I started when I was really little, but I have spent less time playing other board games after I started playing mahjong.
Why do you like board games so much?
Is that so hard to understand? I get to use the rules to torment my opponents. Don't you think games like that are so interesting?
Huh?
It's nothing. You'll experience this kind of fun too. There will be so many ways for us to develop our synergy in the future!
...Are you crazy?

After hearing my request, Chiori Mikami's face is filled with disbelief. She picks up her mobile phone next to her and taps it a few times. Immediately afterward, the door opens with a bang as Riu Kujou storms in angrily.
...Eh? Ah! Not so hard!
After teaching me a lesson, Riu Kujou leaves after Chiori Mikami tells her to.
I'll give you one more chance. Think carefully about your wish.
With lingering fear in my heart, I raise my hand timidly.
It's rare for a lady as proud as Chiori Mikami to take the initiative to show me her cute side. It's obvious that she is doing her best to win this game. How can I ruin this moment with my own hands?
With a soft heart, I go along with Chiori Mikami's act and pretend to be fooled into looking in the direction she is indicating.
What is it?
"Ding!" As expected, Chiori Mikami takes the opportunity to ring the bell.
Oh? Diversionary tactics?
Hehe, there can never be too much deception in war!
Oh well. I won't let you distract me so easily next time!
Although I said that, events have a tendency to repeat themselves. In the next two games, I fail to stop Chiori Mikami from diverting my attention.

By the way, do you still remember the kittens from last time? Riu contacted volunteers later to adopt them... There's Whitey, Blackie, Tangerine... Oh, do you remember the colors of the other two kittens?
Hmm, let me see...
"Ding!" Chiori Mikami takes the chance to ring the bell again.
I'm starving! I really want to eat something. Are you hungry? Tell me what you want to eat. I'll treat you to anything you want to eat today!
...Um... Are you sure I can have anything I want...?
"Ding!" The girl rings the bell yet again.

"Ding!" "Ding!" "Ding!" Behind her words of concern and sweet voice are all kinds of cute traps and the cruel reality that she is ringing the bell before me and that my hand is growing thinner over time...
Finally, after she rings the bell one last time, I lose all the cards in my hand.
Looking at the table, which is empty as I expected, I dumbfoundedly raise my hands to surrender.
Okay, I lose. Your strategy is too good, Chiori. It looks like I won't be able to avoid this game training.
To my surprise, Chiori Mikami isn't as happy as I thought she would be. She pushes the cards she won toward me.
This game doesn't count.
I'm not stupid. {var:player_nickname}, you were going easy on me the whole time.
Taken aback, I scratch my face in embarrassment.
Um... not the whole time. I really was fascinated by your lovelyness, Chiori.
...Hmph, you smooth talker. We're not going tomorrow. The training is canceled.
Eh? Why is that?
...You idiot! You went easy on me because you didn't want to make me sad. I'm such a kind person, so of course I have to think about things from your perspective!
...Since we have different ideas of what counts as winning in that game, if we win my way, you won't be happy as my partner in the game.
T-That's not it! We need to play this game as a team, so we won't really win unless we both think we've won!
So... we'll need to do some real training so that we both win even if we don't go tomorrow.
...Real training?
As if she senses my confusion, Chiori Mikami suddenly gets up, walks to the bookcases, and presses something.

In the next second, I hear the sound of mechanical slide rails as the seemingly normal bookcases suddenly move. Some bookcases move to the left, while some other bookcases move to the right, revealing a hidden space behind them!
You didn't expect this, right? I'm not an ordinary player. If you want to fight alongside me, you need to play as many board games as me first and reach my level.
It turns out that Chiori Mikami hadn't gone to the board game parlor to play one game on a whim. Is she a pro-level expert?
This young lady always seems to surprise me.
Just like that, Chiori Mikami and I promised to play more board games together to develop a deeper rapport.
When I look through her collection of board games carefully, I ask her curiously--
...When I see the sweet smile on Miss Chiori's face, anticipation, and fear emerge in my heart at the same time.
Okay, I have no problem with that if it's for your victory, Chiori. I accept! Let's do it!
Very good. Now start by studying the movements on the board!
Chiori Mikami and I begin to carefully study the rules of this board game that is played in teams of two...
Couple Opponent
Oh... we lost.
Well played.

We come to the board game parlor as agreed and compete with the couple again. Thanks to yesterday's training, the "synergy" between Chiori Mikami and me has improved substantially. Although our opponents have an amazing synergy, it pales in comparison to our 100% perfect understanding.
Since it's the weekend, the best way to rest is naturally to play mahjong at home all day! How can you claim to understand me if you don't know that? Why did you choose to go out?

You idiot, the premise of the current plot is that we are trapped in a forest labyrinth for some unknown reason. Will you consider whether it's the weekend in this situation? Of course you need to make the most of your time and try to find the exit!

Come on, we should take things as they come. Doesn't it say that we can still connect to the Internet? That should mean it isn't that dangerous. If we play mahjong, we might even get a reminder from one of the NPCs we are playing against!
Hah! Your fanciful thinking is beyond my understanding... We'll follow your decision then!

Due to scenarios like those, they ended up making different decisions, which resulted in their game characters entering a dead end in the plot. Alternatively, they wasted too much time arguing about what decision to make and missed many opportunities to get shortcuts.
As a result, we quickly win the board game and escape the labyrinth of Heart Map by reaching the destination.
Chiori Mikami is really happy after winning the game. As she is thirsty, I go to buy her a drink while she is excitedly reflecting on everything that happened in the game.
After I arrive at the vending machine selling drinks in front of the board game parlor, I happened to meet the couple who we just played against. When they see me, they walk over to me quickly.
Although we lost, we had such an amazing experience! It's much better to make the wrong move in a game than in real life. Isn't that right, babe?
Yeah, sometimes losing is a good thing.
Probably because my confusion is too obvious, they start explaining things to me.
We got a lot of new inspirations after losing this game.

Because this board game is created with authentic emotional interactions in mind, the crossroads you encounter while playing Heart Map are real situations that you might encounter with your lover in real life... Without being pushed by external pressure, you might never realize that there are still so many things you need to work out or that your lover might have ideas you never knew about.
Ahaha, I see...

"The relative relationship between winning and losing, huh?" As I listen to their conversation, I seem to remember something I mentioned casually before and realize that there is a deeper meaning I hadn't noticed...
After I wave goodbye to the lovey-dovey couple, I return to Chiori Mikami with two cold drinks.

Chiori Mikami is in a very good mood and is taking a photo of the board game representing her victory so she can make a post on CatChat. Recalling the words of the couple from before, I ask her a question tentatively.
Chiori, do you like this Heart Map game?
Hmm? Do I like it? Um... not particularly. I just heard that this game has been really popular recently. I played it two times, and it's so easy to devise a strategy to win.
I knew it. To Chiori Mikami who is only 14 years old, the concept of "winning from losing and losing from winning" is too difficult to understand.
To the contrary, Chiori Mikami pats me instead.
Yeah, sure.
No, my goal is to win! With a hard heart, I put a stop to Chiori Mikami's cute behavior.
"Ding!" I ring the bell without any hesitation and laugh wildly at Chiori Mikami's stunned expression with my hands on my hips.
Hahaha, are you trying to divert my attention? That's not happening.
Argh! Damn it!
It's useless even if her embarrassment turns to anger. With a heart of stone, I win the game smoothly and steadily.
Hehe, I win. As agreed, you'll have to listen to me now.
Chiori Mikami looks unhappy and unwilling to accept her defeat.

Hmph! Fine then. I didn't expect you to be so good at this too... But I'll only listen to you this one time! I won't lose to you next time! If you give me a little time, I'll definitely win against you in this game!
Pfft... Okay, I'll be looking forward to it.

Sigh, has she made her goal to defeat me instead after giving up on her plan to get revenge tomorrow? Chiori Mikami really is as competitive as ever... In any case, I've achieved my goal this time. There's plenty of time in the future for me to teach her more principles in an appropriate way.
This incident quickly becomes an ordinary event in our daily lives. And when I mention it to her later by chance, she doesn't even seem to remember it.
It should be Geisha coffee.
Hah! You don't even remember the type of coffee I like to drink. I even stated it publicly before.
Congratulations on getting it wrong. You can leave now.
Huh? It's over already?
The question-and-answer session ends abruptly, and I am expelled from their conversation.
On the next day, I see Chiori Mikami's latest CatChat post on my phone.
